paper.title: VELMA: Verbalization Embodiment of LLM Agents for Vision and Language Navigation in Street View
paper.central_claim: VELMA: an LLM agent for urban VLN in Street View that verbalizes the instruction, trajectory and visual observations (landmarks extracted from the instruction by an LLM, scored in five view directions with standardized CLIP similarity, plus intersection info) as prompt text and predicts the next action by next-word prediction; it follows instructions with only two in-context examples and, when LoRA-fine-tuned (incl. response-based learning), achieves 25-30% relative task-completion improvement over the previous state of the art on Touchdown and Map2seq.
paper.claim_type_note: Also modifies the Touchdown environment; central contribution is the agent (A class).

materials.figure_only_content: Fig 5 (KPA vs model size), Fig 4/6 CLIP score distributions; numbers not in text. Dev/test instance counts per dataset not stated.

scope_check.reason: LLM agent (GPT-3/4 few-shot, LLaMA-7b tuned) with CLIP perception harness navigating Street View graph; A class.

signatures.object: Verbalization harness that turns Street View panoramas into text observations for an LLM navigator.
signatures.information: Instruction text; at each step 5 views (left, slightly left, ahead, slightly right, right) of the panorama, intersection count from the navigation graph; no raw pixels reach the LLM.
signatures.operation: GPT-3 extracts landmarks from the instruction once -> CLIP (ViT-bigG) similarity for 'picture of [landmark]' standardized with ~20k training-area panoramas -> thresholded at tau=3.5 -> templates 'There is [l] on your [direction]' / '[N]-way intersection' appended to the running prompt -> LLM predicts the next action.
signatures.conditions: Touchdown and Map2seq in the unseen-area protocol; ~40 steps per route; dev-only for GPT few-shot.
signatures.feedback: New observation text after each executed action.
signatures.selection_rule: argmax next-action word; no verifier or consensus.
signatures.persistence: Full prompt sequence in context within the episode; no cross-episode state.
signatures.claimed_effect: 2-shot GPT-4 dev TC 10.0/23.1; removing the image channel lowers fine-tuned dev TC 23.4 -> 15.0 (Touchdown) and 41.3 -> 37.8 (Map2seq).
signatures.failure_boundary: Only instruction-mentioned landmarks are verbalized; CLIP false positives at the threshold; open LMs reach KPA 48-58 but TC 2-3 in few-shot.

signatures.object: Environment/interface fix: no automatic heading snap on FORWARD, turn semantics relative to all outgoing edges, new TURN_AROUND action.
signatures.operation: Modify state transition so action sequences align with 'turn right at the intersection'.
signatures.claimed_effect: Makes few-shot agents feasible; baseline retrained in the modified environment (ORAR-spade).
signatures.failure_boundary: Comparison against originally published baselines in the unmodified environment is not like-for-like.

signatures.object: Response-based learning (RBL) fine-tuning of LLaMA-7b on its own rollouts with oracle correction.
signatures.information: Student sees verbalized prompts; the oracle (shortest path to the goal) is privileged at training time only.
signatures.operation: With probability 0.5 student-forced rollout: if it stops within one node of the target, its own actions become the reference; otherwise a stepwise oracle gives counterfactual actions along the student's trajectory; else teacher forcing on the gold route.
signatures.selection_rule: Success-gated self reference vs oracle relabel.
signatures.later_use: Used for dev/test rollouts in the held-out area.
signatures.failure_boundary: Single model size; three seeds; oracle-only dynamics.

gap.author_gap: How best to connect LLMs to an interactive visual environment; urban VLN in real Street View has long (40-step), dense-scene trajectories and alignment inconsistencies that prior LLM-based indoor agents and sequence-to-sequence agents do not address.
gap.checked_gap: Plausible and specific (long-horizon outdoor VLN, cannot transcribe every view); the proposed fix is a narrow channel (instruction-mentioned landmarks), so the residual 'what the LLM cannot see' is only partly characterised.
lineage: Indoor LLM agent that transcribes whole images (Zhou, Hong, Wu 2023)
CLIP-landmark route planning (Shah et al. 2022; planned a priori)

closest_adjacent.name: ORAR

closest_adjacent.name: Zhou, Hong, Wu 2023 (LLM indoor VLN)
closest_adjacent.solves: LLM planner over image-to-text transcripts for 6-step trajectories

gap.residue: Open-ended landmark detection reliability, spatial/temporal reasoning, few-shot gap to fine-tuned agents (10/23 vs 26/47).
gap.stakes: Verbalization as a general LLM-embodiment interface.
gap.method_response: Landmark extraction + CLIP visibility + templates + environment alignment fix + RBL fine-tuning.
gap.remaining_gap: Few-shot performance remains low; test-set LLM results absent; no failure analysis.
gap.unresolved: No local pin for the indoor LLM VLN neighbor; novelty beyond the stated first-claim not searched.

matches.reason: Visual observations are serialized into the text surface form of a language model so one next-token objective handles instruction, history and perception.

tactic_steps_checked: recast imitation of gold routes as supervised relabeling of the learner's own visited states by a shortest-path oracle: met for RBL
success_failure_checks: success: unlocks capability native teacher forcing lacks (recovery, stop-near-target): partial
matches.reason: RBL is a DAgger-style supervised relabeling step; C21 (hindsight relabeling of achieved outcomes) is not selected because relabeling targets the true goal, not the achieved outcome.

rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partial: verbalization makes LLM navigation possible, but few-shot TC remains 10/23 and best results need fine-tuning

matches.operation_match: A separate frozen vision-language model (CLIP) converts images into text that the LLM planner consumes.
matches.difference: Converter is a thresholded similarity scorer for instruction-derived landmarks plus templates, not a generative VLM description; no raw-image arm.

condition_checks.note: Text channel vs no-image ablated, but not vs raw images.
CLIP backbone swapped (CLIP vs OpenCLIP), no converter-free upper bound; converter dependent on tau chosen by inspection.
Latency and cost unaccounted; mostly dev-only for GPT.

matches.operation_match: Relabel learner-visited states with a privileged shortest-path expert and train on them DAgger-style.
matches.difference: Student is a verbalizing LLM, not a harness-teacher; success-gated switch to own actions; teacher is a graph oracle, not an LLM harness.

condition_checks.note: Deterministic graph dynamics, so relabeling is viable; RBL +2.9/+7.5 TC over FT on test.
Three seeds with std; thin ablation (no oracle-only or student-only arm).
Early/late STOP errors addressed qualitatively; no endpoint breakdown.

unassigned: Template verbalizer of graph metadata (intersection count) as privileged-but-shared channel.
revision_proposals: Consider documenting that K604 covers non-LLM-teacher oracles in graph environments; no change applied.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Serialize vision into text via a frozen contrastive VLM so a language model can navigate.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions: Text channel measured against raw images (K109 S6); here only vs no-image.
pattern_mapping.differences: CLIP scorer + templates rather than caption generation.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Oracle relabeling of the learner's states is the supervised-relabeling object.

claims.text: Few-shot LLMs follow urban VLN instructions via verbalization.
claims.setting: Touchdown and Map2seq dev sets, unseen area, 2 in-context examples.
claims.baseline_control: FORWARD-only heuristic; LLMs of different sizes; trained ORAR (not matched).
claims.selection_vs_test: GPT results on dev only; tau not tuned.
claims.result_denominator: GPT-4 TC 10.0 / 23.1 vs ORAR-spade dev 21.5 / 32.8; dev instance counts unstated.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Only GPT-3/4 and Mixtral reach substantial dev TC; few-shot is well below trained agents; no test-set few-shot evidence.

claims.text: Fine-tuned VELMA is new SOTA (25-30% relative improvement).
claims.setting: Test sets of both datasets, 3 seeds.
claims.baseline_control: ORAR retrained in the modified environment (ResNet and OpenCLIP).
claims.selection_vs_test: checkpoint chosen on dev; test held out.
claims.allowed_conclusion: VELMA-RBL exceeds a retrained trained baseline by about 32-46% relative TC in the authors' modified environment; the abstract's 25-30% and the 77%/57% claims are not like-for-like.

claims.text: Visual landmark verbalization matters and RBL helps.
claims.setting: Dev sets (image ablation), test sets (RBL vs FT).
claims.baseline_control: no-image, CLIP, OpenCLIP; FT without RBL.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Image channel adds +8.4 / +3.5 dev TC; RBL adds +2.9 / +7.5 test TC over FT; 'less prone to overfitting' is asserted not tested.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop navigation with environment-checked task completion on a real-imagery graph; the geographically separated test area is the benchmark's standard split, not an unused embodiment or simulator.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In the authors' modified Touchdown/Map2seq environment, a LoRA-fine-tuned LLaMA-7b navigating on verbalized CLIP-landmark observations with RBL training exceeds a retrained trained baseline on the held-out-area test sets (TC 26.4 vs 20.0; 47.5 vs 34.0), and 2-shot GPT-3/4 achieve nontrivial dev TC.
assessment.cannot_claim: Like-for-like superiority over previously reported SOTA in the original environment, the 25-30% abstract figure, few-shot test performance, that text observations reduce overfitting, cost viability.

G.reason: Specific, sourced gap (long-horizon urban VLN; per-view transcription infeasible) with the main trained baseline compared, but the closest LLM-agent neighbor is not run and the characterization of what the verbalized channel cannot represent is thin.

M.reason: Verbalization + landmark-visibility interface is a sensible, partly tested response (image ablation, dev gain) and RBL targets the stop/recovery problem; the information bottleneck (only instruction landmarks) and the unproven overfitting explanation limit the argument.

X.reason: Prompt format, scorer standardization, thresholds, templates, extractor prompt, RBL algorithm, LoRA settings and decoding are reconstructable; boundaries and failure modes are not analyzed and the RBL description has an internal cross-reference slip.

measurement.reason: Environment-checked TC/SPD/KPA with a defined success radius and 3-seed results for trained rows, but dev/test instance counts are absent, the success radius is lenient (one neighboring node), few-shot GPT numbers are dev-only without variance, and extraction was only hand-verified on 50 instances.

causality.reason: Vision channel ablation and RBL vs FT use the same model/data with seeds, and ORAR is retrained in the modified environment; confounds remain: LLaMA-7b vs small LSTM, environment changes, untested components (intersections, TURN_AROUND), asserted overfitting explanation.

holdout.reason: Training, dev and test areas are geographically separated, 58% of test landmarks are novel, tau was not tuned and checkpoints are chosen on dev; but scenes/city/benchmark are the same family, few-shot GPT has no test result and LLM pretraining leakage is only mentioned.

statistics.reason: Three seeds with mean and std for all fine-tuned and baseline rows and RBL gains exceed std, KPA partly decomposes failures; few-shot rows lack variance, no tests, no failure categories.

cost.reason: Cost is cited only as the reason GPT is dev-only; trajectory length (about 40 steps, 200 views) is the only compute proxy; no GPU-hours, tokens, latency or budget matching.

status_reason: Complete body and appendices read; all eight ratings resolved.

evidence.quote: achieve 25%-30% relative improvement in task completion over the previous state-of-the-art for two datasets
evidence.support_explanation: Author headline claim; Table 2 test numbers vs retrained ORAR imply +32-46% relative TC, so the abstract figure does not match the table.

evidence.quote: (i) We introduce VELMA, to our knowledge, the first LLM-based agent for urban VLN.
evidence.support_explanation: Author novelty claim; closest LLM VLN neighbor (indoor NavGPT-style) cited only in related work.

evidence.quote: This is feasible because the navigation trajectories are only six steps on average compared to 40 steps in the urban VLN task considered in our work.
evidence.support_explanation: Why indoor image-to-text transcription of every view does not transfer.

evidence.quote: we propose a more intuitive way to solve this ambiguity at intersections
evidence.support_explanation: Environment/interface modification that also enters baseline comparisons.

evidence.quote: The verbalizer is a template-based component that produces environment observations in text form.
evidence.support_explanation: Template verbalizer (intersection count from navigation graph + visible landmarks).

evidence.quote: Extracting this information directly from the navigation graph is akin to the junction type embedding used by the ORAR model
evidence.support_explanation: Intersection information comes from environment metadata, not pixels; same side information as the baseline.

evidence.quote: the landmark is classified as visible in the current view
evidence.support_explanation: Landmark visibility decided by thresholded standardized CLIP score.

evidence.quote: The threshold was selected by inspecting the distribution of CLIP scores (as in Figure 4 ) for a handful of landmarks.
evidence.support_explanation: Single tunable parameter chosen by inspection, not systematically tuned.

evidence.quote: On purpose, we did not systematically tune it in order to not violate the premise of few-shot learning.
evidence.support_explanation: Disclosure on tuning.

evidence.quote: On average, 2.7 landmarks were extracted from a navigation instructions text.
evidence.support_explanation: Landmark extractor output size; extraction run once with GPT-3 and reused.

evidence.quote: For Touchdown we calculated an F1-score of 96.3
evidence.support_explanation: Extractor quality measured on 50 hand-annotated dev instances per dataset.

evidence.quote: This means that generalization is crucial because the training routes are located in an area that is geographically separated from the area of development and test routes.
evidence.support_explanation: Unseen-area protocol for training vs dev/test.

evidence.quote: Around 58% of the landmarks in the test sets are novel
evidence.support_explanation: Novel-landmark rate on test.

evidence.quote: All experiments are repeated three times with different random seeds (mean/std reported).
evidence.support_explanation: Seeds claim; few-shot rows in the table carry no std.

evidence.quote: Due to cost and data leakage concerns, we evaluate the GPT models on the development sets only.
evidence.support_explanation: GPT few-shot results exist for dev only, none on test.
2-shot GPT-4: dev TC 10.0 (Touchdown) and 23.1 (Map2seq); no test numbers.
Fine-tuned LLaMA-7b with gold sequences: test TC 23.5 / 40.0.
Response-based learning: test TC 26.4 +-1.7 / 47.5 +-0.7.
Retrained SOTA baseline in the modified environment: test TC 20.0 / 34.0.

evidence.quote: we additionally retrain ORAR in the improved environment for a fair comparison
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline retrained after the environment change.

evidence.quote: Overall, our contributions in this work amount to a relative increase of task completion by 77% and 57% over the previously reported state-of-the-art for urban VLN
evidence.support_explanation: 77%/57% compare with the originally reported baseline in the unmodified environment (26.4/14.9, 47.5/30.3).
Dev vision ablation with fine-tuned LLaMA-7b: no-image 15.0/37.8 -> OpenCLIP 23.4/41.3 TC.

evidence.quote: We thus train the agent to directly optimize the TC metric while also feeding it its own actions during training, called VELMA-RBL
evidence.support_explanation: Response-based learning (student forcing + oracle correction).

evidence.quote: an oracle path is computed to provide the optimal counterfactual action at each step in the trajectory
evidence.support_explanation: Privileged shortest-path oracle relabels learner-visited states on failure.

evidence.quote: to collect training losses in a batch evenly from both training strategies
evidence.support_explanation: Mixing ratio 0.5 teacher/student forcing.

evidence.quote: The task completion (TC) rate is a binary metric that measures whether the agent successfully stopped within one neighboring node of the target location.
evidence.support_explanation: Success definition (lenient: one neighboring node).

evidence.quote: Each dataset includes around 10k navigation instances
evidence.support_explanation: Dataset scale; dev/test split sizes are not stated.

evidence.quote: However, this KPA score only translates to task completion (TC) rates of 2.1 and 3.2
evidence.support_explanation: Few-shot open LMs: KPA 48-58 but TC 2-3; only GPT-3/4 and Mixtral get substantial TC.

evidence.quote: In contrast, the LLMs in our work act as a blind agent that solely relies on observation descriptions produced by the verbalizer.
evidence.support_explanation: Information channel is the verbalizer only.

evidence.quote: shows that the text-based environment observations are less prone to overfitting
evidence.support_explanation: Asserted explanation for FT vs ORAR; not isolated by an experiment.

evidence.quote: We use Adam ( Kingma and Ba 2015 ) as the optimizer with a learning rate of 0.0003
evidence.support_explanation: Fine-tuning hyperparameters are given (LoRA r=8, 20 epochs, batch 16, greedy decoding).

evidence.quote: The best model is selected by task completion on the development set.
evidence.support_explanation: Model selection on dev; test held out for the final table.
